There was a set menu of chicken doritang + green onion chicken skewers, so I ordered it.
Sides include tteokbokki (you can only choose 1 side if you choose tteokbokki, or 2 sides if you choose rice balls or fried food) and 2 mild green onion chicken skewers.
As if it wasn't enough, I added another green onion chicken skewer menu and ate a total of 6 pieces, 4 of which were spicy.

We went a little earlier than dinner time and the owner seemed busy. It took a while for the menu to come out, but it seemed like it was because they carefully grilled the green onion chicken skewers themselves. The taste was worth the wait. Basically, the meat and green onions gave off a lot of charcoal flavor, the mild flavor was sweet and savory, and the spicy flavor was spicy without being too spicy, so it had a different charm. All the ingredients were cooked well and the meat was chewy and the green onions were delicious.

Tofu kimchi is served as a basic side dish. In addition to that, it also comes with pickled radish and macaroni salad. Water is self-serve. It was nice to have ice to drink cool water or drinks in hot weather.

It's not in the picture, but the tteokbokki served on the side seems to be about 3 cups worth of paper cups from the snack bar in front of the school. It wasn't too spicy and was good enough to whet my appetite.

As I ate the chicken doritang (dakdoritang) from the previous menu, it seemed like the portion was larger than it looked. When the owner took my order, he asked if I wanted to add Cheongyang pepper. I added it, and it was spicy and delicious. One person in my group who doesn't like spicy food found it quite spicy, so I think it would be a good idea to leave that person out. This is the exterior of Baekgeok Salon’s main branch!

​
There are about 4-5 tables outside the store and the cute light bulbs and lights look emotional.

​

Baek Eok Salon’s main branch is located on the second floor of the building.

If you go up the stairs, the store is on your right, and if you take the elevator, get off and turn left.

Maybe it's because the Baekgeok Salon store concept is based on the background of the enlightenment period.
From the entrance, the retro feel of the wallpaper and signboard is noticeable, and the colorful chandelier looks atmospheric.

In line with the enlightenment concept, there are antique wallpapers, mirrors, and chandeliers throughout the store.

The interior clearly shows that the owner put a lot of thought into it, and it was nice because it was a good background for posting Instagram stories.

Basically, there is a table for 4 people inside, and chairs are added to one side to create a table for 5 people.

At the Baekgeok Salon main branch, you can eat together, and there is a separate bar table where you can enjoy a variety of alcoholic beverages such as highballs, sake, Kaoliang liquor, and beer.

There were a lot more different types of sake and Kaoliang liquor than I expected, and because it was a retro concept, it was refreshing that there was no wine.

I think it's nice to have a bar table so you can drink alone without being noticed!

Overall, the store was clean and the two male and female owners were really friendly.

There are room seats on one side of the store, so you can enjoy group gatherings and group dinners privately.

Room seats do not have private doors, but are separated from the table for 4 people.
There is a partition between the two four-person tables.

The bathrooms were separated for men and women, and it was very convenient because it was a store-only bathroom, not a commercial bathroom.

The interior of the men's restroom has a retro feel similar to the store concept and is extremely clean!

This is a terrace with a special outdoor table at Baekgeok Salon Main Branch.
The store is located on the second floor, so it's not that high, and both sides are open, so it's very comfortable!

Also, the cute mini light bulbs hanging on the railings brighten up the mood!

Order the store’s signature menu items, black fried boiled pork and salsal tataki!

I really wanted to try the black fried boiled pork because it is Baek Eok Salon’s signature menu item cooked over an open fire.
My girlfriend’s pick for salchisal tataki!

The batter was black, probably because it was coated in squid ink and then fried.

When it comes to regular boiled pork, it is in the form of boiled pork, but the fact that the boiled pork is deep-fried makes it incredibly fresh.

Basically, boiled pork, flying fish roe, dried radish, and perilla leaves are provided, and a generous amount of garlic sauce is provided.

Does the squid ink fry have a big ink flavor? It didn't taste like that.

The black fried boiled pork was fried on the outside and boiled on the inside, so it was chewy on the outside!

The boiled pork may have a slightly greasy feel because it has batter.
Dried radish, perilla leaves, flying fish roe, and garlic sauce take care of that part.

I can see why the basic ingredients include dried radish, perilla leaves, flying fish roe, and garlic sauce.

The dried radish was not spicy and the perilla leaves were cut into small pieces so it was easy to eat.

The garlic sauce was thick yet savory and light, so it went well with boiled pork!

It was good because there was a lot of garlic sauce so I didn't have to add any additional sauce and I could eat it without worrying about other people.

Next, salchisal tataki!

The price is 24,800 won.

Salchisal that is only cooked on the outside, topped with various vegetables and topped off with yuzu sauce!!!

It was my first time eating tataki, and it was much more to my taste than I expected.

First of all, it had a meaty texture on the outside but a chewy texture like raw meat on the inside, so I loved it!

In particular, the yuzu sauce, which was neither strong nor spicy, and various vegetables were sour and very delicious.

Salchisal tataki that my girlfriend decorated to make it easy to eat.

It was the perfect size for one bite and had a great texture.

Clear black fried boiled pork and salchisal tataki!

Hongdae Restaurant Baek Eok Salon Main Branch is a bar where you can drink and eat.

The atmosphere is so nice that I recommend it as a date spot in Hongdae.

It is a great chicken restaurant with a retro feel that is close to Hongik University entrance and Yeontral Park, making it a great place for gatherings or company dinners. Personally, I think the Hongik University Station Chicken restaurant is good because the surrounding area is less crowded.

There are so many different types of chicken and snacks, so it's great for those who want to eat everything in one sitting, as well as a second bar where you can enjoy a light drink after a meal. There are a lot of cost-effective snacks such as chicken, tteokbokki, various stews, and fried foods, so they are good for any first, second, or third meal. It is also a great place for large gatherings as the group seating is spacious and comfortable.
